summary: Bihani Sarkar works in Indology and religious studies. She has held posts at the University of Hamburg, the University of Leeds (attested 2017 as Teaching Fellow), and Lancaster University (attested 2023-2026 as Senior Lecturer).

Bill M. Mak works in Indology and archaeology. He held posts at Kyoto University (attested 2012; Associate Professor 2014-2019), the Needham Research Institute (2019), the University of Science and Technology of China (Professor 2024), and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Bimal Krishna Matilal was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as Professor at the University of Toronto (~1968-1976) and Spalding Professor at the University of Oxford (1977-1991).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha was an Indologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. from the University of London under Lionel David Barnett. He served as department head at Patna University (1958) and Hon. Jt. Director of K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1968-1977).

Bing Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as a Professor at Sichuan University (~1987) and held a professorial post at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences (attested 1993).

Bingtao Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned an MA from Peking University in 2008 and a PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xue Yu (attested 2015).

Biraja Sankar Guha was an anthropologist and Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University in 1924. He was Director of the Anthropological Survey of India (1945-1954) and later directed the Bihar Tribal Research Institute (1956-1959).

Birgit Kellner is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed her doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura. Her posts include teaching at the University of Vienna and serving as Director of the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2015).
Biscoe Hale Wortham was an Indologist. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge in 1863, and earned his B.A. from Trinity College, Oxford (1863-1868).

Bisheshwar Nath Reu was an Indologist and historian who studied under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. From ~1917 to 1950, he headed the Government Museum Jodhpur and the Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre, and served as Archaeological Superintendent at Sumer Public Library.
Biswajit Biswas is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das and has been a Research Scholar and Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Biswanath Banerjee was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University from 1967 to 1991 and served as president of The Asiatic Society (~1999-2001).
Blain Auer works in Indology, religious studies, and history. He earned his PhD from Harvard University (2002-2009) and became a professor at the University of Lausanne in 2013.

Blanche Christine Olschak was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed a Ph.D. at the University of Graz (~1933-1937) and studied under Constantin Régamey and Thupten Wangyal in 1946.
Bo Jiang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Bo Utas is an Iranian and linguistics scholar who studied at Uppsala University (~1958-1973) under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and Stig Wikander. He served on the faculty at Uppsala University, becoming Professor emeritus (~1987-2003).
Bo-Kwang Han is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at Dongguk University (attested 2004 and 2015).
Bohumil Sládeček was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Charles University's Faculty of Arts (~1902-1908), earning a Ph.D. under the supervision of Josef Zubatý.

Bojan Čop was a linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Ljubljana, where he studied under Karel Oštir. He spent his career at Ljubljana, serving as Assistant in Classics (1949) and Professor of Comparative Indo-European linguistics (1972-1990).
Bokar Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1960-1989). He held a post at Bokar Monastery from ~1984 to 2004.
